body: This breaks the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract. Its Javadoc says it "Never returns {@code null}", but it now returns null when the group is deleted concurrently. The value goes into `GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount`. A client can't tell a null there apart from 'count not requested' (GroupSearchTest asserts `nullValue()` for that case), and any caller that unboxes it will just move the NPE somewhere else. Consider returning `0L`, or better, have the listing code skip groups that disappeared, so a deleted group isn't returned as a phantom entry.

This fix only covers the reported symptom. The same race (cached entry exists, DB row already deleted, so `getGroupModel()` returns null) still throws an NPE in all three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads (lines 256, 262, 268), which call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without a null check. The same sort of concurrent read (e.g. fetching subgroups or group children while groups are being deleted) will still fail. Handle null consistently here too, e.g. return `Stream.empty()`, or use a shared helper.

The reader thread is never joined, so the test is weak and may leak a thread. (1) Nothing guarantees the thread has even started, let alone overlapped with the deletions, before `deletedAll` is set, so the test can pass without exercising the race. (2) The in-flight request can still fail after line 155, and that exception gets added after the assertion at line 157 has run, so it is lost. (3) If `remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set and the thread keeps hitting the server for the rest of the suite. Use an executor or `Thread` with `join()` in a try/finally, and consider a latch so the reads are running before deletion starts.

Does this call actually reach `getSubGroupsCount()`? It only does if the endpoint defaults `subGroupsCount=true` for this overload. Otherwise the test doesn't cover the changed code path at all, so it's worth passing the flag explicitly. Also, `groupUuuids` has a typo (extra 'u'), and the ArrayList filled from `forEach` is fine only because it runs single-threaded.
